answer: Yes. tools/lib/workspace.py runs a network:none unit inside unshare --net with a TUN blackhole as the only uplink. The unit process calls socket.connect with no declaration check; the SYN is observed on the TUN sidecar (out-of-band log) and rejected with an injected TCP RST (errno 111). The same canary succeeds when the unit declares network access, and also succeeds under an assertion-only NETWORK=none env flag, proving documented restriction is not enforcement. Host iptables/nft were not modified. SUCCESS:TST-0225

signals.claim: The TUN sidecar log contains the TCP SYN to the same destination:port; this log is not produced by the unit.

findings.notes: Observed TCP SYN from 10.254.0.2 toward the live canary listener, RST-injected by the sidecar. Not a credential.

negative_controls.description: Setting NETWORK=none in the environment without unshare must still reach the listener. If this control were silent, a documented-only restriction could fake a pass.
On one live listener, network:allowed connects and network:none is RST-rejected with an OOB SYN log.

notes: G-1 TST-0225: live named probes exit 0, receipt state=SUCCESS, per-unit manifest row. Did not run global unit_manifest.py --write. Did not manipulate host firewall. SUCCESS:TST-0225
owner_approval_notes: Catalog marks this unit owner-gated because a host-firewall manipulation would change host netfilter state. This delivery does not touch host iptables/nft; isolation is a throwaway network namespace plus a TUN blackhole owned by the harness.
